recommendations.risk: Medium. Shutdown waiting and health exposure require an explicit timeout and compatibility decision; retries or stronger delivery guarantees would be separate behavior changes.

result.rationale: Good, well-tested domain library with clear separation from runtime effects. Planning, redaction, model-response conversion and reporting have distinct responsibilities (rust/crates/tb-stream-audit/src/lib.rs:26-33; src/plan.rs:8-11; src/archiv.rs:13-15). Configuration remains process-global, and the migration to end-of-stream notifications left maintenance debt (rust/crates/tb-stream-audit/src/config.rs:144-161; rust/bin/tb-stream-audit/src/main.rs:3390-3394). Assessment is against 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, not a complete defect review. Every recommendation is class C, without implementation approval.
strengths: Low runtime coupling: the assigned crate depends on the shared load crate and utility libraries, not HTTP or SQL clients; process execution remains outside the archive helpers (rust/crates/tb-stream-audit/Cargo.toml:6-14; rust/crates/tb-stream-audit/src/archiv.rs:157-206).

Existing components are reused rather than rebuilt: last.rs re-exports tb_load, and the runner uses tb_llm::complete with an explicit timeout instead of a separate model HTTP client (rust/crates/tb-stream-audit/src/last.rs:8; rust/bin/tb-stream-audit/src/main.rs:2956-2964; rust/crates/tb-llm/src/hub.rs:917-934).

Privacy rules are centralized: detection and redaction share compiled patterns; outgoing model requests redact text and replace identifying segment IDs. Raw quotations are excluded from serialization, with an actual regression test (rust/crates/tb-stream-audit/src/rules.rs:54-75; src/llm.rs:144-157; src/lib.rs:95-96,271-280).

State decisions are explicit and testable: queued and in-progress blocks both keep a run open; retries have deadlines and limits; interrupted capture is separate from incomplete model evaluation (rust/crates/tb-stream-audit/src/plan.rs:170-188,206-213,298-310; src/report.rs:48-65).

File sizes are reasonable for the domain library: plan.rs has 910 lines but its test section starts at 490; report.rs has 704 lines with tests from 450. The substantial render function spans 103-212, rather than a multi-thousand-line production module (rust/crates/tb-stream-audit/src/plan.rs:490; src/report.rs:103-212,450).

The archive switch and remote-model permission are intentionally different contracts. Likewise, the audit's data-export permission and the shared hub's endpoint admission check are separate protections, not redundant gates to remove (rust/crates/tb-stream-audit/src/archiv.rs:23-31; src/llm.rs:81-94; rust/crates/tb-llm/src/hub.rs:311-331).
weaknesses: Configuration is fragmented across direct environment reads in config, archiv, llm and melden. The typed Konfiguration does not capture all operational settings, while broker endpoint and credential-resolution policy also exists in tb-config with different normalization details (rust/crates/tb-stream-audit/src/config.rs:144-161; src/archiv.rs:92-99,131-135; src/llm.rs:86-94; src/melden.rs:39-82; rust/crates/tb-config/src/lib.rs:168-182).

The notification migration left an orphaned block-report formatter in the reviewed Rust snapshot and inert block-send scaffolding. dm_text and ende_dm_text repeat the finding-body format, while the runner's dm_senden always succeeds and end notifications use dm_rohtext instead. External consumers of the public library API were not established (rust/crates/tb-stream-audit/src/report.rs:302-355,368-418; rust/bin/tb-stream-audit/src/main.rs:2544-2593,3390-3394,3691-3694).

Domain states rely on publicly mutable strings and flags: categories, severity and confidence are Strings, while block processing combines nur_melden, counters and deadlines. Model normalization helps, but internal invalid combinations remain representable (rust/crates/tb-stream-audit/src/lib.rs:85-97; src/plan.rs:52-74; src/llm.rs:243-264).

Completeness is modeled at block level but not retained in the run aggregate. LaufAkte records counts, findings and time bases, not model failures or interrupted blocks; consumers cannot derive aggregate completeness from that object alone (rust/crates/tb-stream-audit/src/report.rs:48-65,424-442).

strengths: Clear separation between transport contract, network implementation, and intentional headless implementation. Payload types distinguish rich messages, alerts, and DMs; the crate does not incorporate database orchestration (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/backend.rs:7-59,108-135; src/noop.rs:14; rust/bin/tb-bot/src/wiring.rs:599-603,668-684).

One shared HTTP client and POST helper centralize authentication, operation-specific idempotency, and a two-attempt retry limit. Redirects and inherited proxies are disabled, with explicit origin/path validation (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:235-279,284-342).

The large relay file is not a single oversized production function: 900 of its 1,686 lines belong to the test module, and its longest production method spans 61 lines (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:471-531,787-1686).

No orphan source module was found inside the package: lib.rs declares all implementation modules and the relay test module includes personal_invite_tests.rs. Alert/DM separation and the stricter personal-invite origin contract are intentional, not redundant implementations (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/lib.rs:3-5; src/relay.rs:491-498,763-765,789,1529-1562).

Configuration is injected into the transport rather than read from the environment inside it. Consumer settings already have typed validation, and existing domain ports isolate member fetching and directory operations outside the transport (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:235-245; rust/crates/tb-config/src/discord.rs:113-186; rust/bin/tb-bot/src/chat_wiring.rs:2483-2502; oauth_followups.rs:130-143).
weaknesses: HTTP-status/body handling is repeated across methods, while success semantics differ: role mutations return status-only success, message sends expose an unchecked ok field, create operations validate envelopes, and user resolution maps failed envelopes to absence. This makes contract changes harder to apply consistently; it is not a confirmed runtime defect (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:355-386,514-530,619-627,708-773).

The error model mixes local validation failures and malformed responses into BrokerError with synthetic HTTP statuses; reqwest JSON decoding travels through Http. A consumer additionally recognizes a broker condition by substring matching the body, creating text-level coupling (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/backend.rs:97-103; src/relay.rs:250-254,360,449-465; rust/bin/tb-bot/src/wiring.rs:508-514).

Origin validation happens when an operation is called, not when BrokerRelay is constructed. Timing policy is fixed at 10 seconds/two attempts/two-second waits, with separate 15-second overrides for two GET operations. These are bounded defaults, but they limit early configuration feedback and deterministic timing tests (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:31-33,235-255,643,666).

relay.rs holds DTOs, validation, generic HTTP mechanics, several operation families, and most tests in one module. result.rationale: Solid implementation with clear limits. Shared identity handling, transactional state changes, and meaningful regression tests provide a good foundation. Repeated settings plumbing, inconsistent error handling, and request-time construction of globally configured dependencies prevent a 4. recommendations.proposal: C: Consolidate the two actual departner database implementations behind one existing owning module, preserving separate API authorization and broker/Discord side effects.
recommendations.benefit: Removes an explicitly documented two-place maintenance obligation for sensitive lifecycle flags.
recommendations.risk: Medium to high. Preserve opt-out precedence, administrative blocks, pause cleanup, outcome data and each caller's side-effect contract. This is not permission to merge different safety policies.

recommendations.proposal: C: Separate access-state fetching from pure derivation with an explicit clock. Reuse and carefully extend the existing domain status foundation where appropriate, while keeping display status and access policy distinct.
recommendations.benefit: Makes the repeated base-state interpretation easier to compare and enables deterministic grace-boundary tests without duplicating the state vocabulary again.
recommendations.risk: Medium. Unknown values, precedence and access-specific grace behavior must retain their current contracts.

recommendations.proposal: C: Define explicit partial-completion and degraded-read contracts for best-effort paths before changing them. Distinguish unavailable data from genuine empty or zero results, and make ignored optional-write failures observable.
recommendations.benefit: Improves diagnosis of partially applied lifecycle actions and degraded dashboard data without assuming every optional error should abort the operation.
recommendations.risk: Medium to high. Changing error propagation, atomicity or response shapes can change behavior and requires a separate design decision.

recommendations.proposal: C: Standardize existing DB suites on the already available isolated PostgreSQL helper where suitable, or on a consistent explicit required-DB/skip contract. Prefer migration-backed fixtures where practical.
recommendations.benefit: Makes test evidence easier to interpret and reduces repeated schema setup and fixture drift. This reuses existing infrastructure rather than introducing another test framework.
recommendations.risk: Low to medium. The isolated helper requires PostgreSQL 16 binaries; adoption must retain local portability and does not establish a new mandatory-testing policy.

recommendations.proposal: C: Split streamers_crud internally by lifecycle/identity commands and reporting queries, retaining current public exports. Update layer and legacy-proxy comments to describe the actual Rust boundaries.
recommendations.benefit: Reduces navigation and review effort without proposing a wholesale crate redesign or treating test-file length as production complexity.
recommendations.risk: Low to medium. Preserve public types, JSON contracts and SQL behavior; use re-exports to avoid unnecessary caller changes.

result.rationale: Solid, with clear limits. recommendations.proposal: C: Add a small behavioral worker test seam with explicit time and mocked external responses, then test the composition of persistence, POST, cancellation, degraded health, and restart uncertainty. Retain existing layer tests.
recommendations.benefit: Highest-value assurance improvement: verifies side effects and persisted outcomes rather than relying on source-text ordering.
recommendations.risk: Medium. Keep the seam narrow and preserve the existing unknown-before-send protocol and all protection gates.

recommendations.proposal: C: Standardize database-test fixtures and make omitted integration coverage explicit. Reuse the existing isolated PostgreSQL fixture or required-database helper rather than building another mechanism.
recommendations.benefit: Makes test evidence reproducible and avoids apparently successful runs that never exercised database contracts.
recommendations.risk: Low to medium. Isolated PostgreSQL adds tooling and startup requirements; do not substitute production database access.

recommendations.proposal: C: Separate pure advertising policy, persistence responsibilities, and observation clients into focused modules; extract worker phases without changing their order or transaction boundaries.
recommendations.benefit: Reduces change coupling and the amount of code that must be understood to modify one concern. Makes the store's Steam network dependency explicit.
recommendations.risk: Medium to high. Lease ownership, raid checks, history writes, and non-idempotent POST ordering are load-bearing and must remain unchanged.

recommendations.proposal: C: Introduce typed reason, plan-fitness, action-source, and completion-status values at internal boundaries. Preserve database strings and add bounded diagnostic categories for unavailable Steam observations.
recommendations.benefit: Enables exhaustive handling and clearer diagnosis while retaining the current conservative advertising behavior.
recommendations.risk: Medium. Existing serialized values and database constraints must remain compatible; diagnostic failures must never certify a safe advertising window.

recommendations.proposal: C: Share only a pure, normalized advertising-snapshot mapping and checked numeric conversion. Keep the six-hour collector and manager's change-throttled transactional writer separate.
recommendations.benefit: Reduces mapping drift between two live writers and state projection while reusing the already-existing timestamp normalizer.
recommendations.risk: Low to medium. Preserve invalid-time semantics, sampling cadence, and the manager's atomic snapshot-plus-history-marker update. This is not a recommendation to unify distinct safety contracts.

recommendations.proposal: C: Preserve a typed Result<Option<Credentials>, CredentialError> through credential lookup and uploader resolution, retaining compatibility wrappers where required.
recommendations.benefit: Distinguishes missing connections from storage/decryption failures and makes diagnosis and recovery decisions testable.
recommendations.risk: Medium. Changing error classification can change queue behavior; specify intended handling before implementation.

recommendations.proposal: C: Separate upload orchestration responsibilities and extract a typed TikTok status decoder used by immediate polling and background reconciliation. Preserve their distinct reservation and consent contracts.
recommendations.benefit: Reduces the large process function and prevents status interpretation from drifting between recovery paths.
recommendations.risk: Medium to high. Existing unknown-operation and no-second-upload guarantees must remain unchanged.

recommendations.proposal: C: Make provider transport policies explicit and reuse the existing HTTP-policy helper where contracts match, rather than introducing another client layer.
recommendations.benefit: Makes timeouts, redirect handling and endpoint trust easier to audit consistently.
recommendations.risk: Medium. Provider upload origins, resumable responses and literal-loopback test endpoints require different treatment; do not blindly standardize all requests.

recommendations.proposal: C: Resolve provider configuration once at the composition boundary and inject it together with existing cipher/client dependencies. Preserve current alias precedence and secret-manager storage boundaries.
recommendations.benefit: Improves deterministic testing and avoids configuration behavior being distributed across capabilities, OAuth and disconnect.
recommendations.risk: Medium. Alias compatibility and unavailable-platform behavior are product contracts; protocol constants should not become arbitrary tunables.

Layoutverträge sind ausdrücklich dokumentiert. Neue Eingaben werden streng validiert, gespeicherte Altlayouts gezielt normalisiert; beide Wege verwenden denselben Parser. Das sind unterschiedliche notwendige Verträge, keine unnötige Doppelimplementierung (rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/layout.rs:3; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/layout.rs:214; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/layout.rs:225; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/layout.rs:238).

Der aktive Branding-Renderer besitzt sein exklusives Assetverzeichnis, beendet den eigenen FFmpeg-Prozess beim Future-Drop und veröffentlicht die Ausgabe erst nach erfolgreichem Render durch rename. Fehler und Abbruch sind gezielt getestet (rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/video_processor.rs:29; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/video_processor.rs:345; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/video_processor.rs:364; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/video_processor.rs:377; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/video_processor.rs:726; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/video_processor.rs:774).

Vorhandene Testbarkeit und Wiederverwendung: Downloader sind über ein Trait austauschbar, Medienprogramme über Konstruktoren injizierbar, und der kleine STT-Adapter verwendet den bestehenden Engagement-Client statt eines zweiten HTTP-Clients (rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/preview.rs:174; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/video_processor.rs:320; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/transcription.rs:5; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/transcription.rs:29).

Die STT-Service-Referenz verwendet geprüfte Snapshot-Konfiguration und trennt HTTP-Verarbeitung von blockierender Inferenz. Ein Semaphore begrenzt parallele Decoder; Kontext-STT nutzt denselben Client mit einem ausdrücklich lokalen Vertrag (rust/bin/tb-stt-server/src/main.rs:59; rust/bin/tb-stt-server/src/main.rs:205; rust/bin/tb-stt-server/src/main.rs:306; rust/bin/tb-stt-server/src/main.rs:316; rust/crates/tb-config/src/stt.rs:72; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/clip_context_harvest.rs:502).

weaknesses: Das Fehlermodell unterscheidet mehrfach nicht zwischen fehlenden Daten und kaputter Infrastruktur: Layoutleser verlieren SQL-/Parsefehler als None beziehungsweise Fallback, der Vorschau-Claim verliert SQL-Fehler als leere Arbeitsliste, Template-Anwendung liefert nur bool. Bei DB-Problemen fehlen damit hilfreiche Ursachen und differenzierte Reaktionen (rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/layout.rs:403; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/layout.rs:470; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/preview.rs:129; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/preview.rs:143; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/clip_templates.rs:178; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/clip_templates.rs:254).

Das Vorschau-Zustandsmodell ist weitgehend implizit: Statuswerte sind Strings, ein Claim wird nur durch Clip-ID und Zeit repräsentiert, und Abschlussupdates tragen keine Identität des konkreten Renderauftrags. Erneute Anforderungen und Wiederaufnahme nach 15 Minuten sind deshalb schwer als eindeutige Übergänge zu modellieren und zu testen (rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/preview.rs:14; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/preview.rs:33; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/preview.rs:95; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/preview.rs:123; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/preview.rs:136).

Prozessgrenzen sind uneinheitlich. render_branded besitzt Abbruchsicherung, aber keine Wall-Clock-Zeitgrenze; das vorgelagerte ffprobe hat weder eine eigene Zeitgrenze noch kill_on_drop. Vorschauaufträge laufen sequenziell. Bereits vorhandene Audio-/Kontextpfade zeigen dagegen Timeout plus Prozessabbruch (rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/video_processor.rs:363; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/video_processor.rs:385; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/preview.rs:234; rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/transcribe.rs:232; rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/transcribe.rs:239; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/clip_context_harvest.rs:55).

Verbliebene öffentliche Altpfade erhöhen die Pflegefläche: convert_and_trim und compose_and_trim werden innerhalb des geprüften Rust-Korpus nicht mehr von Produktaufrufern verwendet; build_clip_ass und subtitles_enabled_for_clip erscheinen nur noch in ihren Tests. Die Modulbeschreibung behauptet weiterhin einen Center-Crop-Uploadpfad. Wichtiges Gegenargument: Das aktuelle Wiring schaltet Clip-Anreicherung ausdrücklich ab, und der Uploadtest erwartet ausdrücklich keine Transkriptworte. Das ist kein Nachweis eines fehlenden Features und kein Anlass zur Reaktivierung (rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/video_processor.rs:5; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/video_processor.rs:588; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/video_processor.rs:623; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/render.rs:11; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/render.rs:29; rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:1713; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/upload_worker.rs:1656).

Die Layoutleser duplizieren SQL-Abfrage, Override-Priorität und Deserialisierung. Ihre unterschiedlichen Rückgabeverträge sind sinnvoll und müssen erhalten bleiben; nur der gemeinsame Lese-/Auflösungskern ist tatsächlich doppelt (rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/layout.rs:456; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/layout.rs:461; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/layout.rs:507; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/layout.rs:512).

Konfiguration ist nur teilweise vereinheitlicht: Vorschauintervall, Batchgröße und maximale Dauer sowie Medienprogramm-Defaults sind lokal festgelegt. Konstruktoren erlauben zwar Programminjektion, das Bot-Wiring nutzt für die Vorschau jedoch die Defaults. Der ungenutzte Enrichment-STT-Adapter startet weiterhin über ENV, während Service und Kontext-STT bereits typisierte Konfiguration verwenden (rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/preview.rs:19; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/preview.rs:163; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/video_processor.rs:310; rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:1703; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/transcription.rs:14; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/clip_context_harvest.rs:502).

Die großen Dateien vereinen Modell/Geometrie, Persistenz beziehungsweise Prozessausführung und Tests. Die Größe ist aber kein Beleg für riesige Produktionsfunktionen: layout.rs umfasst 1102 Zeilen, davon 508 im Testteil; video_processor.rs umfasst 1091 Zeilen, davon 386 im Testteil. Ein gezielter Schnitt wäre hilfreicher als pauschale Größenkritik (rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/layout.rs:595; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/video_processor.rs:706).

Sie rufen nicht PreviewWorker::run_once/render_one auf und prüfen weder parallele Anforderungen während eines Renders noch Wiederaufnahme abgelaufener Claims. recommendations.proposal: C: Eine gemeinsame, parametrisierbare Prozessausführungsregel für die aktiven Medienaufrufe vorsehen. Bestehende Timeout-/kill_on_drop-Bausteine nutzen, statt einen weiteren unabhängigen Wrapper zu bauen; Branding-Publikation und temporärer Besitz bleiben eigene Verträge.
recommendations.benefit: Hoher Betriebsnutzen: Hängendes ffprobe oder FFmpeg kann einen sequenziellen Vorschau-Durchlauf nicht unbegrenzt aufhalten. Einheitliche Zeitbudgets und Fehlerkategorien erleichtern Diagnose und Tests.
recommendations.risk: Mittel. Zeitgrenzen verändern Verhalten bei langsamen, bisher erfolgreichen Medienprozessen. Budgets müssen ausdrücklich festgelegt werden; lokale STT- und andere Sicherheitsverträge dürfen nicht verwischt werden.

recommendations.proposal: C: Infrastrukturfehler als Result erhalten und fachliche Zustände getrennt modellieren. Layout-Abwesenheit, ungültige gespeicherte Daten und DB-Ausfälle unterscheiden; Vorschauabschlüsse einem konkreten Auftrag zuordnen.
recommendations.benefit: Hoher Diagnose- und Wartungsnutzen: Ein DB-Ausfall sieht nicht wie eine leere Queue oder fehlendes Layout aus. Wiederholte Anforderungen und Wiederaufnahme lassen sich als prüfbare Zustandsübergänge beschreiben.
recommendations.risk: Mittel bis hoch. Rückgabeverträge und möglicherweise das Jobmodell ändern sich. Erwartete Fallbacks müssen erhalten bleiben; eine Änderung der Persistenz könnte eine Migration erfordern. Keine automatische Umsetzung.

recommendations.proposal: C: Die vorhandenen Tests gezielt um vollständige Vorschauabläufe, abgelaufene Claims, erneute Anforderungen während eines Renders und erfolgreiche reale Medienausgabe ergänzen. Vorhandene Downloader-Injektion und Fake-Programme weiterverwenden.
recommendations.benefit: Hoher Absicherungsnutzen bei geringem Umbau: Verknüpfungen zwischen DB-Zustand, Download, Render und Veröffentlichung werden geprüft, nicht nur einzelne Helfer. Der aktuelle Vertrag ohne Transkript-Untertitel bleibt Ausgangspunkt.
recommendations.risk: Niedrig bis mittel. DB- und echte FFmpeg-Tests benötigen ausdrücklich verfügbare Fixtures und passende Plattformen. Nicht jede Qualitätsprüfung muss zu einem obligatorischen Runtime-Test werden.

recommendations.proposal: C: Den aktiven Rendervertrag und bewusst stillgelegte Enrichment-/Subtitelpfade klar kennzeichnen. Nach Prüfung öffentlicher API-Verbraucher ungenutzte Center-Crop-/Trim-Ketten gegebenenfalls aus der aktiven Pflegefläche nehmen; keine Transkription reaktivieren.
recommendations.benefit: Mittlerer Nutzen mit zunächst geringem Risiko: Wartende sehen sofort, welcher Pfad tatsächlich läuft. Veraltete Kommentare und Tests mit irreführenden Namen erzeugen weniger falsche Annahmen.
recommendations.risk: Dokumentationsabgleich niedrig, Entfernung öffentlicher APIs mittel. In-repo fehlende Aufrufer beweisen keine externe Nichtverwendung. Die ausdrücklich abgeschaltete Anreicherung und separat bestehende Kontext-STT dürfen nicht verwechselt werden.

recommendations.proposal: C: Den gemeinsamen Layout-Lese-/Auflösungskern extrahieren und Modell/Geometrie von SQL-Persistenz trennen. Die APIs für gespeichertes Layout und effektives Fallback sowie die strenge und kompatible Validierung ausdrücklich getrennt erhalten.
recommendations.benefit: Mittlerer Wartungsnutzen: Änderungen an Override-Priorität oder DB-Abfrage müssen nicht zweimal nachgezogen werden. Die großen Dateien werden übersichtlicher, ohne notwendige Vertragsunterschiede zu beseitigen.
recommendations.risk: Niedrig bis mittel. Ein unvorsichtiger gemeinsamer Rückgabewert könnte fehlendes Layout und Fallback gleichsetzen oder Altlayout-Kompatibilität ändern. Bestehende Roundtrip- und Prioritätstests sind wichtige Gegenkontrollen.

All recommendations are class C.

recommendations.proposal: C: Separate tracker observation/ownership state, socket driving and SQL persistence into independently testable components. Consider sharing narrow IRC IO primitives, but preserve AnonymousChat's token-free, restricted-write API and the distinct membership protocol.

recommendations.risk: Medium: public return types and caller handling would change; this is not authorization to alter failure or retry behavior.

weaknesses: The main orchestration method combines admission, conversation persistence, roughly a dozen context sources, prompt construction, model execution, session bookkeeping and live side effects. Most database collaborators and the rhythm guard are constructed internally, limiting isolated tests. File size alone is not the concern: pipeline.rs contains 502 lines from its test section onward, but handle_gated itself still spans 356 lines (rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/pipeline.rs:91-139,199-554,557).

Generation and confirmed delivery are not represented as separate lifecycle states. The pipeline updates rhythm, assistant memory and thread references before returning Spoke; the caller sends afterward, through an Option<bool> result. This makes a generated answer, a dropped answer and a delivered answer difficult to reconcile across layers (rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/pipeline.rs:518-552; rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/stealth_sender.rs:92-112,164-193; rust/bin/tb-bot/src/chat_wiring.rs:1793-1812).

Error reporting is uneven despite the good LLM error enum. Channel discovery and learning-window reads turn database errors into empty collections; profile rebuilds collapse model/storage failures into None; decision-log insertion ignores its result. Missing data and failed infrastructure therefore often have the same outward shape (rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/background.rs:66-77; rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/reaction_learning.rs:719-770; rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/channel_background.rs:137-151; rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/gate.rs:134-151).

Generic transport mechanics are duplicated. Both IRC readers implement anonymous handshake, welcome/PING handling and JOIN/PART writing; StealthSender manually implements a Helix chat POST and response interpretation even though tb-transport-twitch already offers that operation and typed outcomes. The business policies and identities remain different and should not be merged (rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/irc_reader.rs:170-224,348-410; rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/learn_irc_reader.rs:95-143,205-240; rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/stealth_sender.rs:148-193; rust/crates/tb-transport-twitch/src/chat.rs:22-32,295-303).

Configuration is fragmented across database settings, environment lookups and constants. Rhythm has injectable values, but the pipeline always constructs it from defaults/environment; learning caches enablement and owner at construction while reading several limits later; background intervals are hardcoded. Reproducing one effective configuration requires following several modules (rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/rhythm.rs:34-48; rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/pipeline.rs:123; rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/reaction_learning.rs:147-180,272-299,318-331; rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/background.rs:35-49).

recommendations.proposal: C: Reuse the existing shared database-configuration reader and strengthen database contract tests. Retain both timestamp compatibility fixtures, add a migration-backed ad-context case, and add deterministic concurrent lifecycle cases.
recommendations.benefit: Improves confidence in schema compatibility and concurrency while reducing divergent test setup and misleading database-free success.
recommendations.risk: Low to moderate if test-only. Do not flatten intentionally different fixtures or replace isolated schemas with shared mutable state.

recommendations.proposal: C: Introduce structured lifecycle and enrichment outcomes that distinguish missing data, database failure, already-finalized state and degraded completion. Preserve current best-effort behavior unless separately approved.
recommendations.benefit: Makes operational diagnosis and failure-path tests more precise without inferring that all auxiliary failures should block session completion.
recommendations.risk: Moderate: return-type changes affect callers. Changing retries or whether incomplete metrics are persisted would require a separate behavioral decision.

recommendations.proposal: C: Split telemetry normalization, ad-context enrichment and business side effects into focused components behind the current facade. Preserve subscription transaction atomicity and moderation ordering.
recommendations.benefit: Reduces cross-domain coupling and makes policy branches easier to test independently of SQL and mutable chat state.
recommendations.risk: Moderate: a purely organizational split can still alter transaction or side-effect timing. Subscription reminders and moderation enforce different contracts and must not be merged into a generic fire-and-forget mechanism.

recommendations.proposal: C: Plan consumer-led consolidation of the main and experimental session representations. First document output equivalence and sampling differences; retain an adapter or separate projection wherever experimental consumers need distinct semantics.
recommendations.benefit: Could remove parallel lifecycle/cache maintenance and reduce future aggregate drift without abandoning existing analytics endpoints.
recommendations.risk: High: affects historical data, timestamp precision, numeric types and reader contracts. Requires migration/product approval and is not a cleanup or immediate fix.

result.rationale: Solid foundations with clear limits. Polling has explicit effect ports, live-state writes are transactional, and login reconciliation has substantial regression coverage. However, the transition coordinator is large, discovery bypasses the existing source abstraction, and outcomes blur failures with deliberate skips. These limits prevent a 4/5 assessment. recommendations.proposal: C: Extract a pure per-channel transition decision from process_entries, leaving effect execution and persistence in explicit phases. Preserve the distinct polling, EventSub and guard contracts.
recommendations.benefit: Makes restart, reconnect and pending-announcement combinations reviewable independently of database and transport orchestration.
recommendations.risk: Medium to high: ordering and carry-forward semantics are behavior-sensitive. Existing restart/recovery assertions must remain authoritative.

recommendations.proposal: C: Give scout an injectable source seam using the existing StreamSource capabilities, and consolidate the two Helix snapshot mappings at an appropriate adapter boundary. Add full-cycle discovery fault tests before changing lifecycle behavior.
recommendations.benefit: Reduces concrete transport coupling and mapping drift while making category failures, absence counting and removal sequencing directly testable.
recommendations.risk: Medium: retain scout's separate sampling policy and explicitly decide integer-conversion behavior rather than assuming the current mappings are identical.

recommendations.proposal: C: Make orchestration outcomes explicit: distinguish already-current/skipped edits from failed edits, and represent retrieval completeness and cleanup results instead of only maps or void returns.
recommendations.benefit: Improves recovery reasoning and diagnostics without requiring a blanket rewrite of transport or SQL error types.
recommendations.risk: Medium: changing how incomplete discovery data influences removals is a separate behavior decision, not an automatically authorized fix.

recommendations.proposal: C: Reuse one database-test prerequisite contract across integration and inline tests, including the existing required-database check. Evaluate the already available isolated PostgreSQL helper instead of inventing another fixture framework.
recommendations.benefit: Prevents selected database regressions from appearing successful merely because their prerequisite was absent, and reduces duplicated setup policy.
recommendations.risk: Low to medium: stricter prerequisites expose environment failures previously skipped; migration to isolated PostgreSQL needs compatible schema fixtures.

recommendations.proposal: C: Separate or retire deliberately dormant role-provider and poller-reminder APIs after checking compatibility requirements; reconcile comments and startup logs with actual typed configuration and current wiring. Do not reactivate these paths.
recommendations.benefit: Reduces misleading extension points and accidental duplicate reminders while retaining the intentional no-role-ping behavior.
recommendations.risk: Low for documentation/log corrections, medium for public API removal. Existing feature-disabled contracts must remain unchanged.

result.rationale: Solid implementation with clear maintenance limits. Explicit validation, transactional session ownership and meaningful database tests are strengths. Large multi-purpose stores, duplicated low-level helpers, silent degradation in learning reads and inconsistent test prerequisites prevent a 4. recommendations.benefit: Reduces the amount of unrelated state a maintainer must understand for one lifecycle change.
recommendations.risk: Medium: preserve worker cancellation, queue visibility and archive ordering exactly; this is a separate refactoring proposal, not a fix.

recommendations.proposal: C: Extend the existing injection pattern to audit adapters and finite controller steps, then add deterministic tests for transcription/model failure, broker acknowledgments and restart sequencing.
recommendations.benefit: Tests the service's decisions across boundaries rather than only its helpers and shared transports.
recommendations.risk: Low to medium: avoid production-only abstractions or replacing already tested clients; test seams should preserve existing behavior.

recommendations.proposal: C: Encapsulate marker reading/writing behind explicit lifecycle operations and distinguish missing, malformed and unreadable state with typed errors, building on the existing outcome enums.
recommendations.benefit: Makes recovery decisions and operational diagnostics inspectable without tracing scattered booleans, JSON values and String errors.
recommendations.risk: Medium to high: retain existing marker names, JSON schemas, legacy compatibility and conservative retention semantics; migration is not authorized.

recommendations.proposal: C: Document and isolate the legacy per-block notification compatibility path, then consider retiring its dormant failure/retry machinery only after persisted-state compatibility is proven.
recommendations.benefit: Removes misleading active-path expectations without confusing aggregate end delivery with the retired per-block behavior.
recommendations.risk: Medium: legacy marker recovery remains reachable; removing it blindly could alter handling of existing recordings.

recommendations.proposal: C: Consolidate validated non-secret runtime configuration and policy defaults behind one explicit interface, preserving the separate remote-data permissions and credential contracts.
recommendations.benefit: Makes effective configuration and precedence easier to inspect and test while reducing scattered ENV access.
recommendations.risk: Medium: preserve launcher precedence, existing defaults and any intended runtime re-reading; credential and permission contracts must remain distinct.

strengths: Klare Betriebsgrenze: ausschließlich Rust, ein dauerhaft geladener Whisper-Kontext, separat gekapselte Recovery und Inferenz im Blocking-Worker statt direkt im asynchronen Handler. Die Semaphore begrenzt native Inferenz auf einen Lauf (rust/bin/tb-stt-server/src/main.rs:10,193-210,316-321; ops/stt-server/README.md:18-26).

Typisierte STT-Konfiguration mit Loopback-Pflicht, Wertebereichen, unbekannte-Felder-Ablehnung und expliziter Remote-Ausnahme. Der Server übernimmt den validierten Snapshot und meldet dessen Fingerabdruck (rust/crates/tb-config/src/stt.rs:14-31,72-138; rust/bin/tb-stt-server/src/main.rs:59-88,158-175).

Gut ausgearbeitetes Recovery-Zustandsmodell: Startgeneration und Karenz, wachsendes Backoff, begrenzte Warnmeldungen, erneute Zustandsprüfungen vor try-restart sowie atomare, synchronisierte Persistenz. Die wiederholten Prüfungen haben einen Schutzvertrag und sind keine unnötige Dopplung (rust/bin/tb-stt-server/src/recovery.rs:94-159,298-325,380-491).

HTTP-Fehler werden zentral abgebildet; interne Details bleiben aus der 500-Antwort heraus. Der vorhandene Client besitzt klassifizierte Transport-, Timeout-, HTTP- und Decode-Fehler (rust/bin/tb-stt-server/src/main.rs:135-153; rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/transcribe.rs:64-77,293-308,386-402).

Vorhandene Bausteine werden wiederverwendet: Whisper und VAD nutzen denselben Downloadhelfer; der Social-Media-Adapter delegiert an OpenAiTranscriber statt eine zweite Transkriptionspipeline zu implementieren. Keine belastbare große Pfaddopplung in den gelesenen Quellen (rust/bin/tb-stt-server/src/main.rs:177-190,475-536; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/transcription.rs:9-25,30-56).

Die Größe von recovery.rs ist nicht mit einem 1264-zeiligen Produktionsmonolithen gleichzusetzen: Das große Testmodul beginnt bereits bei Zeile 501. Die eigentlichen Abläufe sind in benannte Funktionen für Proben, Zustandsübergänge und Persistenz zerlegt (rust/bin/tb-stt-server/src/recovery.rs:163,205,267,311,380,417,501-502).
weaknesses: Die Kernfunktionen sind stärker gekoppelt als die Recovery: main.rs vereint Start, HTTP-Vertrag, WAV-Decodierung, native Inferenz, Segmentfilter und Modelldownload. Engine enthält unmittelbar WhisperContext; die vorhandenen drei Servertests prüfen lediglich WAV-Form und Defaults, nicht den realen Handler oder Downloadpfad (rust/bin/tb-stt-server/src/main.rs:92-100,157-231,265-536,539-592).

Die Semaphore begrenzt nur Inferenz. Upload und PCM-Decodierung erfolgen vor dem Warten auf den Permit; im gelesenen Handler fehlen eine explizite Begrenzung wartender Jobs und eine Wartefrist. Der native Blocking-Lauf hat außerdem keinen sichtbaren Abbruchvertrag. Das erschwert nachvollziehbares Verhalten bei mehreren langsamen Anfragen, ohne hier einen Laufzeitdefekt zu behaupten (rust/bin/tb-stt-server/src/main.rs:279-289,304-321).

Gemeinsame Dateikonfiguration ist noch nicht durchgehend wirksam: Server und neuer Clip-Kontext verwenden SttConfig, andere produktive Aufrufer weiterhin den ENV-Konstruktor mit eigenen Defaults. Konfigurationsherkunft und Zeitbudgets müssen daher pro Aufrufer ermittelt werden (rust/bin/tb-stt-server/src/main.rs:59-88; rust/crates/tb-social-media/src/clip_context_harvest.rs:502-516; rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/transcribe.rs:27-36,150-164; rust/crates/tb-engagement/src/background.rs:295-302; rust/bin/tb-bot/src/outreach_shadow_wiring.rs:225-228).

recommendations.risk: Medium. Status strings are persistence and cross-service contracts; changing their serialized representation or fallback behavior would require a separate decision.

recommendations.proposal: C: Finish the configuration boundary for genuinely operational, nonsecret values and inject already-resolved credential dependencies into construction. recommendations.proposal: C: Provide a reliable dedicated entry point for the existing synthetic Uplink interaction proof, and extend interaction coverage to rotation confirmation, OAuth return and disconnect retries. Preserve browser-policy boundaries and existing executable verification.

recommendations.proposal: C: Establish an explicit lifecycle decision for the standalone Hochkant and YouTube Live components. Treat them as intentionally staged modules if that is the plan; integrate or remove them only under a separate approved product decision.

recommendations.proposal: C: Add an explicit parity check for named TypeScript/Rust profile values, or derive both from a shared machine-readable catalog. Keep server-side validation and platform capability checks independent.

recommendations.risk: Low to medium. User-visible wording and recovery behavior require separate approval; do not expose sensitive upstream errors.

recommendations.proposal: C: Extract channel-scoped query/mutation orchestration and the large tab/card implementations from SocialMedia.tsx, retaining existing contracts and query identities.
recommendations.benefit: Makes state ownership, cache invalidation and individual interactions easier to understand and test without changing product behavior.
recommendations.risk: Medium. Callback closures, channel remounting and mutation-result attribution must remain unchanged.

recommendations.proposal: C: Define an explicit editor-to-dialog dirty/busy contract using the existing unsaved-state mechanism. Keep TikTok consent semantics separate; any changed close/confirmation policy requires a deliberate product decision.
recommendations.benefit: Lets navigation and dialogs observe the real lifecycle of layout and metadata editing instead of unrelated mutation state.
recommendations.risk: Medium. Close, reset, focus restoration and pending-save behavior are user-visible.

recommendations.proposal: C: Reuse one channel-specific VOD settings controller across the full settings card and archive toggle. Preserve the distinct admin all-channel list scope and privacy controls.
recommendations.benefit: Centralizes read-error protection, mutation feedback and cache updates for the same setting without removing either useful view.
recommendations.risk: Low to medium. Do not conflate channel settings with the authorized all-channel archive listing.

recommendations.proposal: C: Add mounted VOD interaction coverage alongside existing tests, and make the browser fixture's built-asset input explicitly attributable to the reviewed commit. Replace source-extraction assertions incrementally with behavior assertions.
recommendations.benefit: Covers asynchronous UI wiring that render/backend tests cannot establish and makes future test results attributable to source rather than an unidentified external bundle.
recommendations.risk: Low for product behavior; moderate test-harness work. Preserve existing queue, consent and partial-save regressions.

recommendations.proposal: C: Classify the unconsumed frontend label/API exports as intentionally reserved or removable, then narrow the frontend surface accordingly. Do not infer backend-route removal from missing dashboard consumers.
recommendations.benefit: Reduces misleading parallel filter vocabulary and distinguishes actual UI consumers from merely available API wrappers.
recommendations.risk: Low for local labels, higher for API exports until other consumers and intended maintenance workflows are checked.

result.rationale: The 4/5 rating remains justified. call_endpoint coordinates several sensitive phases, but transport, response parsing and ledger persistence are already separate helpers. Its 186 lines support an optional orchestration cleanup, not a claim that architectural separation is absent.

result.rationale: Retain 3/5: solid with clear limits. Independent fixed-SHA reading confirms duplicated deactivation rules, inconsistent role-outcome consumption and competing test-only analytics handlers, balanced by reusable stores, explicit ports, centralized guards and meaningful regression assertions. Two recommendations need narrowing because domain response models and validated configuration snapshots already exist. All recommendations remain class C; nothing was implemented or promoted to a security finding.
corrections: The manual-raid and scam HTTP ports return unrestricted JSON, but their production implementations already serialize structured ManualRaidResponse, RevokeOutcome and EnforceOutcome values. The limitation is type erasure at the port boundary, not an absence of domain result models. Reuse or relocate existing contracts rather than introducing parallel models.

Configuration validation and immutable snapshots already exist. Handler-level global access is a dependency-injection limitation, not missing validation or an ENV-based operating configuration system. Narrow recommendation 5 to passing an appropriate view of the existing snapshot and grouping composition dependencies.

The link-candidate fallback logs database failures. Its limitation is that HTTP consumers cannot distinguish failure from an empty result, not a complete absence of observability. Database-backed tests also already print SKIP and support TB_TEST_REQUIRE_DB; recommendations should reuse these mechanisms.
accepted_recommendations: C1: Consolidate ownership of the shared deactivation database transition, preserving adapter-specific responses, operation ordering and distinct activation, verification, signup-block and raid-exclusion policies. This has the strongest demonstrated maintenance benefit; compatibility risk is medium to high.

C2: Prioritize consuming RoleRevokeOutcome consistently and adding inspectable role-grant outcomes. If action ports become typed, reuse the existing manual-raid and scam response contracts without creating dependency cycles. Preserve external JSON, OAuth status conventions and best-effort semantics. Risk is medium.

C3: Add focused signup-block and invite adapter tests through build_internal_router, plus representative production-stack replay and partial-failure cases. Reuse existing fixtures, doubles and TB_TEST_REQUIRE_DB rather than duplicating storage or idempotency suites. Risk is low to medium.

C4: Partition streamer ports, HTTP adapters and orchestration into focused modules. Audit consumers before retiring the three superseded analytics handlers and their local test routes; update demonstrably stale comments. Their absence from the inspected production router is established, but universal orphan status is not. Organizational risk is low; deletion risk is medium.

C5: Consider a named composition dependency bundle and explicit injection of the existing validated configuration snapshot or relevant subset. This is a lower-priority testability refinement, not a new configuration system. Preserve restart-only activation, separate security policies, optional-port behavior and Axum extractor contracts. Risk is medium.

corrections: The detail adapter does not discard the OAuth response completely: raw retains the entire payload. The precise weakness is that StreamerDetail has no typed oauth member and the page reads OAuth fields from settings, although Rust emits them separately. Existing DTOs and normalizers should be acknowledged rather than describing the frontend as wholly untyped.

Draft loss is conditional on a refreshed detail object changing the effect dependency. Invalidation alone does not prove that every action overwrites drafts. A changed Discord response resetting an unsaved plan draft is supported by the shared effect and invalidation path.
accepted_recommendations: C: Prioritize the detail oauth/settings contract and explicit response decoding within the existing API client. Preserve legitimate form and JSON protocol differences.

C: Reuse OperatingConfig's draft/baseline separation and existing Scopes/BotControl load/error presentation. Define per-panel reset semantics rather than forcing every form into one generic abstraction.
